text:
Elena: Oncall reported operators can't trace why a rollout fell back. UI just shows 'fallback' with no context.
Jorge: Backend still emits event_id (evt_3222223333) but we removed it from the client after security concerns.
Priya: UX suggestion: a small 'Why did we switch?' flyout that shows rule name + trigger + sample flag + one sanitized example.
Sam: Backend can mint an opaque trace_token and return sample_rate + trigger_counts. Token resolves on the server and checks ACL before returning the audit row. Example: {trace_token: tkn_7f4, sample_rate: 0.05, trigger_counts: {timeout:3}}
Priya: UI detail: rollout header shows `Fallbacks: 3 sampled / 24 total` with tooltip about sampling. Flyout lists rule version, trigger window, sampled? yes/no, sanitized_example (first 40 chars + ...).
Elena: Ops also complained about confusing degrade labels like 'soft-cut'. Propose canonical names: Graceful (lower quality), Failover (switch endpoint), Silent (cache response). Add 1-line microcopy and icons.
Sam: Implementation note: store hash(event_id)->event_id mapping server-side; mint HMAC(trace_token) with short TTL (24h). Token endpoint validates user auth and ACL. No raw PII in token.
OpsBot: audit service mapped evt_3222223333 -> https://audit.redwood/evt_3222223333 (requires SSO and role check). :lock:
Elena: Action items: Sam -> trace_token + counts + small histogram endpoint. Priya -> flyout mock + label copy + icons. Jorge -> confirm audit mapping flow with security.
Sam: ETA: basic trace_token + counts by Thu EOD; histogram next week.
Priya: I'll have mocks Wed and a feature-flagged branch by Fri for small operator beta.
Elena: Sync Thu 10am to hand off. Goal: make fallbacks explorable without exposing PII.
Sam: :thumbsup:
Priya: :+1:
